day_to_day.name: Haiya
day_to_day.description: Shop in front of Sakitsu Church famous for limited handmade traditional rice sweets and fig jam.

day_to_day.name: Takaramochi Honpo
day_to_day.description: Amakusa shop making and selling additive-free koppa mochi of dried boiled sweet potato, mochi rice, and sugar.

day_to_day.name: Aesop Confectionery
day_to_day.description: Makes Amakusa specialty sweets aka-maki and nanban yokan, sold at its factory antenna shop.

day_to_day.name: Amakusa Fisheries Sakitsu Direct Sales Kintsu Market
day_to_day.description: Fisheries shop selling fresh Sakitsu and Amakusa seafood, dried fish, fish paste, grilled noble scallops, and homemade meals.

day_to_day.name: Goshoura Shiosai-kan Local Products Hall
day_to_day.description: Local products hall beside Goshoura Hongo Port selling island seafood, produce, and souvenirs, with ferry tickets and information.

day_to_day.name: Tokyu Workshop
day_to_day.description: Kiln selling simple white, black, and green everyday dishes. New works appear at May holiday and autumn equinox kiln openings.

day_to_day.name: Roadside Station Amakusa City Dolphin Center
day_to_day.description: A roadside station in Itsuwa on northern Amakusa Shimoshima, offering dolphin-watching reception, seafood products, and a restaurant.

day_to_day.name: Ichiyama Kujiraya
day_to_day.description: Workshop and gallery of potter Ichihara Fumiko, independent since 2010, showing handmade tableware and small goods.

day_to_day.name: Maruo Ware
day_to_day.description: Historic kiln founded in 1845, displaying everyday ceramics glazed to a recipe kept since the third generation.

day_to_day.name: Roadside Station Miyajidake Kakashi no Sato
day_to_day.description: Roadside station in a former school in Amakusa's Miyajidake, displaying more scarecrows than the town's population.

activities.name: Ariake Onsen Sazanami no Yu
activities.description: Onsen center by Roadside Station Ripple Land, with open-air baths viewing Shiroga Beach, the Ariake Sea, and Mount Fugen.

activities.name: Shimoda Onsen
activities.description: Onsen on Amakusa Shimoshima with East China Sea views and undiluted 40-42 degree natural water.

activities.name: Sumoto Onsen Center Kappa Romance Hall
activities.description: Kappa-faced onsen with cypress scent. Radon-rich alkaline simple spring, family baths, sauna, outdoor bath, and Japanese garden.

activities.name: Natural Onsen Aimuri
activities.description: Spanish-style sodium bicarbonate onsen. Large, outdoor, and four family baths, plus indoor pool and restaurant. Fully barrier-free.

activities.name: Dolphin Watching
activities.description: See about 200 wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins off Amakusa year-round, with over 90 percent encounters.

activities.name: Nagomiyado Shinwaso Kaishin
activities.description: Small 10-room seaside inn at Amakusa Shimoshima entrance, with fresh fish dinners and a hiba-wood private bath.

activities.name: Gunpokaku Gracia
activities.description: Taisho-romantic Japanese-modern Shimoda Onsen ryokan with five rooms, stained glass, and three free-flowing hot springs.

activities.name: Ajinoyado Kaiotei
activities.description: Inn at Amakusa Shimoda Onsen with plentiful hot water; the owner, an active fishmonger, serves live fish.

activities.name: Amakusa Shimoda Onsen Boyokaku
activities.description: Ocean-view hotel facing Amakusa's west coast, with free-flowing natural onsen and seafood dinners.

activities.name: Relaxation Inn Marco
activities.description: Onsen inn a five-minute walk from the sea, with free-flowing baths and Amakusa seafood.

activities.name: Igaya
activities.description: Meiji-founded ryokan in Shimoda Onsen with smooth free-flowing baths and seasonal seafood.

activities.name: Amakusa Shimoda Onsen Yunohana Travel Inn
activities.description: Inn overlooking the East China Sea, with free-flowing onsen and dolphin-watching package plans.

activities.name: Amakusa Olive Farm AVILO
activities.description: Experience olive farm on a hill in Itsuwa, growing ten varieties, with tours, hand-pressing, and tastings.

activities.name: Ishiyama Rikyu Gosoku no Kutsu
activities.description: All-detached onsen inn in Unzen-Amakusa National Park overlooking the East China Sea, with 15 villas and Amakusa kaiseki.

activities.name: Ebisu Beach
activities.description: Quiet 267-meter white-sand beach facing the Shiranui Sea, watched over by four Ebisu statues.

activities.name: Shirogahama Beach
activities.description: 515-meter white-sand beach with gentle waves, popular with women and families, facing Unzen.

activities.name: Demon Castle Park
activities.description: Demon theme park in Itsuwa, Amakusa, with a 13-meter observatory tower overlooking Hayasaki Strait.

activities.name: Takahama Ware Juho Kiln
activities.description: Historic kiln started in 1762. Takahama ware is white, thin, and translucent. Offers visits, painting, and a museum.

activities.name: Ushibuka Marine Park Glass Boat Submarine
activities.description: Semi-submersible boat from Ushibuka fishing port, five trips daily, about 80 minutes. View the seabed; feed seagulls in winter.

activities.name: Ubushima Campground and Beach
activities.description: Uninhabited-island white-sand beach and campground, five minutes by boat from Kamihira Port. Bungalows but no electricity.

activities.name: Hondo Beach
activities.description: Quiet, shallow beach looking toward Unzen. Popular with families, with showers, changing rooms, and a rest area.

activities.name: Kotakahama Beach
activities.description: Small, gentle beach inside Yokaku Bay, recommended for children. Toilets, showers, changing rooms, and a first-aid station without lifeguards.

activities.name: Satsuki Beach
activities.description: Crescent beach with one kilometer of sand and a wheelchair ramp. Family-friendly, with a beach festival in season.

activities.name: Shiratsuruhama Beach
activities.description: A 1.3 km white beach like a crane's wings, one of Japan's 100 best. Clear water, surfing, and sunsets.

activities.name: Mogushi Beach
activities.description: Natural beach 15 minutes from central Ushibuka. Clear color-changing water; turtles nest May-June. 2003 NHK drama site.

activities.name: Onikizaki Beach
activities.description: East China Sea beach with superb sunsets and clear water. A sandy shore appears from the sea at low tide.

activities.name: Tachiumi Beach
activities.description: Shallow, calm southeast Shimoshima beach facing Yatsushiro Sea. Fish visible. Popular with young children. Wooden toilets and showers.

activities.name: Gosoku no Kutsu Literary Promenade
activities.description: A 3.2 km trail on the 1907 route of five Myojo poets, about two hours, with viewpoints and poem boards.

activities.name: Kuroshima Uninhabited Island
activities.description: Uninhabited island 10 minutes by charter boat from Goshoura. White beach, camping, toilets; a spring well is not drinkable.

activities.name: Ushibuka Haiya Festival
activities.description: April's third Saturday and Sunday festival, with about 5,000 Haiya dancers and a fisheries fair.

activities.name: Wakamiya Park Beach
activities.description: Calm family beach backed by Mount Unzen, with Kame Island walkable at low tide.

activities.name: Tsujishima
activities.description: Small island home to wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins, with dolphin watching and salt workshops.

activities.name: Perla no Yubune Aibo no Yu
activities.description: Natural hot springs at Hotel Alegria Gardens Amakusa, with sea-view and forest baths plus five private baths.

activities.name: Amakusa Cultural Exchange Center
activities.description: A spot to experience making Amakusa crafts, housed in a Western-style nationally registered tangible cultural property.

activities.name: HIGH BEACH
activities.description: Near Shiratsuruhama Beach, offers Amakusa herb distillation and aroma craft experiences. Opened in 2018 by aromatherapist Miho Kurosawa.

activities.name: Kuratake Sunny Auto Campground
activities.description: Winter-comfortable campground overlooking the Amakusa islands, with hands-free camping sets and gear rental.

activities.name: Amakusa Ushibuka Onsen Yasuragi-so
activities.description: Quiet Ushibuka onsen inn with 14 rooms, fresh local fish, Amakusa Daio chicken, and natural hot springs.

activities.name: Amakusa West Coast Holiday Park Furaibo
activities.description: Campsite, whole-house guesthouse, and cottages on an Amakusa west-coast inlet, seven minutes from Shimoda Onsen, with powered RV sites.

sights.name: Ushibuka Kaisaikan
sights.description: Sea-culture complex under Ushibuka Haiya Bridge by the ferry terminal, with shops, exhibits, a 1,000-fish tank, and a restaurant.

sights.name: Catholic Sakitsu Church
sights.description: Symbol of Sakitsu village, a 2018 World Heritage Hidden Christian site; Gothic church rebuilt in 1934 with rare tatami floors.

sights.name: Catholic Oe Church
sights.description: Earliest Amakusa church after Christianity's ban ended; 1933 building by Father Garnier and local believers.

sights.name: Ebisu Statue Park
sights.description: Park with Japan's largest marble Kuratake Great Ebisu statue, weighing 320 tons.

sights.name: Thirteen Buddhas Park
sights.description: Park famed for sunset views from Myokenura to Shiratsuruhama Beach, with Yosano poetry monuments.

sights.name: Myokenura (Elephant Rock)
sights.description: Nationally designated scenic natural monument reef on Amakusa's west coast, linked by sea caves.

sights.name: Tsuten Park Ai yori Aoku Monument
sights.description: Park just past Tsuten Bridge, with a monument to the 1972 NHK drama set in Ushibuka.

sights.name: Tomiyama Narcissus Park
sights.description: Summit park over Ushibuka Port with about 450,000 narcissus, one of Amakusa's eight sunset views.

sights.name: Tsuruhayama Park
sights.description: Park on Amakusa's southernmost cape, overlooking Nagashima in Kagoshima, with about 1,000 cherries.

sights.name: Gion Bridge
sights.description: One of Japan's largest stone girder bridges, a national Important Cultural Property built in 1832.

sights.name: Ushibuka Haiya Bridge
sights.description: 883-meter bridge over Ushibuka fishing port, designed by Renzo Piano and lit at night.

sights.name: Ushibuka Park
sights.description: Circuit-style Japanese garden around a former reservoir, also one of Japan's 100 urban parks.

sights.name: Martyrdom Park
sights.description: Park on former Hondo Castle site overlooking Hondo, with a memorial mound and spring cherry blossoms.

sights.name: Meitoku-ji
sights.description: Amakusa's first Zen temple, built after the rebellion by magistrate Suzuki Shigenari to spread Buddhism.

sights.name: Amakusa Collegio Museum
sights.description: Museum showing Nanban materials, including a restored Gutenberg press from the Tensho embassy.

sights.name: Amakusa Kirishitan Museum
sights.description: Museum of Amakusa Christian history in four zones, showing about 200 items including Shiro's battle flag.

sights.name: Itsuwa History and Folklore Museum
sights.description: Displays stone tools and pottery from Okinohara Shell Mound, plus Edo fishing gear and Jomon salt-making tools.

sights.name: Ogase and Kogase
sights.description: Dozens of wave-carved reefs about 1 km off Shimoshima. Ogase holds tropical sea life; Kogase draws shore anglers.

sights.name: Oidake Observatory
sights.description: Observatory on Oidake, Amakusa's second-highest peak at 582 meters. Views of islands, Aso, and Fugendake. Drive-up access.

sights.name: Tsujishima Wind Power Plant
sights.description: Clean-power wind turbines on Tsujishima symbolize Itsuwa Town. Traditional seawater salt-making continues, and dolphins visit.

sights.name: Nigaki Fossil Park
sights.description: About 20 touchable shell fossils from 100-million-year-old Goshoura strata. Iron dinosaur sculpture; nearby ammonite layer.

sights.name: Amakusa Rosary Museum
sights.description: Museum of Amakusa hidden Christians' life and faith, with Maria Kannon, relics, a recreated hidden room, and films.

sights.name: Ueda Family Residence and Ueda Museum
sights.description: Historic Ueda headman-house museum of Amakusa documents and old Takahama ware; interior closed.

sights.name: Seaside Maria Statue
sights.description: Maria statue near Sakitsu where fishermen pray; its sunset is one of Amakusa's Eight Sunset Views.

sights.name: Sakitsu Village
sights.description: Hidden Christian heritage fishing village where Buddhism, Shinto and Christianity coexisted, with a Gothic church.

sights.name: Nishinokubo Park
sights.description: Rare iris garden on terraced fields, with 250,000 irises and 6,000 hydrangeas in June, plus about 480 cherry trees.

sights.name: Kuratake Shrine
sights.description: Shrine atop 682-meter Mt. Kuratake, Amakusa's highest peak, built to pray for safe fishing.

sights.name: Nishihira Camellia Park (Laputa Tree)
sights.description: About 20,000 wild camellias and a 20-meter tree rooted on a giant rock, called Amakusa's Laputa.

sights.name: Tsukinoshima
sights.description: Uninhabited island with a crescent white beach, popular for diving in Ushibuka Marine Park.

sights.name: Kuroishi Coast
sights.description: Coast where orange sunsets sink into the sea, selected for Japan's Top 100 Sunsets.

sights.name: Makishima Island
sights.description: One of three uninhabited islands in Goshomachi, Amakusa, with Genpei legends of Heike fugitives and Yoshitsune hiding a boat.

sights.name: Kamikake Falls
sights.description: Among Amakusa's largest falls, 15m wide and high after a 700m uphill walk, with Fudo Myoo and access behind.

sights.name: Helmet Plum of Enkei-ji
sights.description: Plum tree over 500 years old, linked to a late-1500s battle legend and said still to bear no fruit.

sights.name: Sakitsu Suwa Shrine
sights.description: A shrine traditionally founded in 1647 for bountiful catches and maritime safety, where hidden Christians secretly prayed.

sights.name: Amakusa City Sakitsu Museum Minatoya
sights.description: A museum introducing Sakitsu village, a component of the Nagasaki and Amakusa Hidden Christian heritage.

sights.name: Amakusa Municipal Goshoura Dinosaur Island Museum
sights.description: Museum on Goshoura Island with about 2,000 fossils from 100-million-year-old strata and life-size dinosaur skeletons.

sights.name: Aoi Aso Shrine
sights.description: Founded in 806; main halls built in 1610-1613 are National Treasures. A Kengo Kuma hall opened on site in 2023.

sights.name: Eikoku-ji
sights.description: Soto Zen temple founded in 1408, famous for a ghost scroll and as Saigo army headquarters.

sights.name: Ganjo-ji
sights.description: Sagara family temple founded in 1233; its seated Amida is a national Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Hitoyoshi Castle Ruins
sights.description: One of Japan's 100 famous castles and a national historic site, Sagara center for about 700 years.

sights.name: Sekisui-ji
sights.description: Temple with a round gate hollowed from a huge stone, plus a spectacles bridge and spring.

sights.name: Kannon-ji Kannon (Kyushu Sagara 33 Kannon)
sights.description: 13th stop of the Sagara 33 Kannon pilgrimage, at a Rinzai temple founded in 1385.

sights.name: Kiyomizu Kannon (Kyushu Sagara 33 Kannon)
sights.description: First Sagara 33 Kannon stop; Thousand-armed Kannon invited from Kyoto Kiyomizu-dera in 1603.

sights.name: Sekishitsu Kannon (Kyushu Sagara 33 Kannon)
sights.description: Seventh Sagara 33 Kannon stop, moved from Sekishitsu-ji after a 1502 quarrel left that temple abandoned.

sights.name: Murayama Kannon (Kyushu Sagara 33 Kannon)
sights.description: Ninth Sagara 33 Kannon stop, whose wooden Thousand-armed Kannon is said to understand people's troubles.

sights.name: Hitoyoshi Castle History Museum
sights.description: History museum of Hitoyoshi Castle.

sights.name: Nagata (Ashihara) Kannon Hall (Kyushu Sagara 33 Kannon)
sights.description: 11th Sagara 33 Kannon stop; image kept in a nail-free, vividly colored late-Edo cabinet.

sights.name: Kuma Shochu Museum Hakutake Densho-gura
sights.description: Museum on 400 years of Kuma shochu history and culture, with exhibits and tasting.

sights.name: Benitoriyama Observatory
sights.description: Overlooks the Hitoyoshi-Kuma Basin, with fantastical mist views in winter. Maintained roads allow access by car.

sights.name: Hitoyoshi Loop Bridge
sights.description: Loop bridge on National Route 221 near the prefecture border, opened in 1977. Length 1,190 m; highest pier 60 m.

sights.name: Kaname Falls
sights.description: Selected among Japan's 100 waterfalls: male about 36 m, female about 30 m, and a gentle fall. Summer retreat.

sights.name: Nuno Falls
sights.description: Named for water wrapping the rock face like a large cloth. Late-July festival offers somen noodles and sweetfish catching.

sights.name: Akaike Kannon
sights.description: 33rd Sagara 33 Kannon site at Akaike Castle ruins. Sho-Kannon, said to be Muromachi, is a city-designated important cultural property.

sights.name: Iwaya Kumanoza Shrine
sights.description: Formerly called Iwaya Gongen, a shrine retaining Shinto-Buddhist syncretism. Its tuff torii and main hall are National Important Cultural Properties.

sights.name: Yunomoto Kannon
sights.description: Eighth Sagara 33 Kannon site near Hayashi Onsen source. The statue was lost in the 1965 flood and replaced.

sights.name: Yasegatsuru Kannon
sights.description: Third Sagara 33 Kannon site. The Eleven-faced image was carried out and enshrined here after the 1862 fire.

sights.name: Mikkahara Kannon
sights.description: Fourth Sagara 33 Kannon site, worshipped since the Edo period. Breast-shaped offerings are said to improve milk production.

sights.name: Sagasato Kannon
sights.description: Sixth Sagara 33 Kannon site, an Eleven-faced image dated 1752. Said to protect children and houses from fire.

sights.name: Sebara Kannon
sights.description: Tenth stop of the Sagara 33 Kannon pilgrimage, founded in 1653 as a retirement temple.

sights.name: Oikami Shrine
sights.description: Deity enshrined in 807; the 1628 hall built by Sagara Nagatsune is a National Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Indo Kyukei Monument
sights.description: Built November 1, 1953 to honor Hitoyoshi-born lyricist Indo Kyukei, writer of Kokyo no Haika and Ryoshu.

sights.name: Yatake Station
sights.description: Closed. Highest station on the Hisatsu Line mountain section, at 536.9 m, with a Meiji building and D51-170 display.

sights.name: Okoba Station
sights.description: Closed, including the restaurant. Japan's only station with both a loop and switchback; many business cards are posted.

sights.name: Hitoyoshi Plum Garden

sights.name: Nishize Bridge
sights.description: Model for the anime Natsume's Book of Friends, with Kuma River sunset views and crested kingfishers.

sights.name: SL Observatory
sights.description: Viewpoint for Japan's only working stone engine shed, built in 1911, with a nearby turntable viewing zone.

sights.name: Misogi Bridge
sights.description: 1921 three-arch bridge called the prefecture's oldest concrete bridge, before Aoi Aso Shrine.

sights.name: Kajiyamachi Street

sights.name: Kumamoto Prefectural Traditional Crafts Center
sights.description: Center displaying prefecture-designated traditional crafts, with a sales corner and local folk toys.

sights.name: Kumamoto Crafts Hall
sights.description: Hall displaying and selling traditional and contemporary crafts, with demonstrations and experience programs. Temporarily closed.

sights.name: Shimada Art Museum
sights.description: Art museum in a quiet bamboo grove holding nearly 1,000 samurai-culture antiques, including Miyamoto Musashi items.

sights.name: Kumamoto Prefectural Museum of Art Annex
sights.description: Renovated former prefectural library with modern design, mainly used as a rental venue for local exhibitions.

sights.name: Kumamoto Prefectural Museum of Art Main Building
sights.description: Comprehensive museum in Kumamoto Castle Ninomaru Park displaying Kumamoto antiques, modern Japanese art, and Western works.

sights.name: Sokeien Garden
sights.description: Former Murai family villa garden beside Chokoen, with a curving spring-fed stream, fireflies, and autumn leaves.

sights.name: Suizenji Kyosai Kaikan Gracia
sights.description: Ten-minute walk from Suizenji Station, near Suizenji Jojuen, with a peaceful Japanese garden and a summer beer garden.

sights.name: Kumamoto Museum
sights.description: General museum of Kumamoto memory, showing Important Cultural Properties, history, and nature, plus workshops and a planetarium.

sights.name: Kumamoto City Museum of Contemporary Art
sights.description: Urban museum in a central complex, with galleries, an art library, kids' atelier, and barrier-free access including braille and elevators.

sights.name: Hanaokayama Buddhist Reliquary Tower
sights.description: 133m mountain north of JR Kumamoto Station, said to have the city's finest night views, with a white stupa.

sights.name: Myokai-ji Ruins and Hosokawa Family Mausoleum (Kitaoka Nature Park)
sights.description: 1642 Hosokawa family temple later opened as a park with gardens and successive lords' mausoleums.

sights.name: Shirakawa Wakuwaku Land (Shirakawa Chiiki Bosai Center)
Meihachi Bridge
sights.description: Stone bridge over the Tsuboi River by Hashimoto Kangoro, now for pedestrians and bicycles only.

sights.name: Chokoen Garden
sights.description: Mid-Edo Hosokawa villa garden, open by the owner's courtesy, with a pond and spring water.

sights.name: Taniozaki Plum Grove Park
sights.description: Park of about 300 plum trees, said to have been a military plum field under Kato Kiyomasa.

sights.name: Kumamoto City Water Science Museum
sights.description: Hands-on learning center on groundwater, water supply, and sewage, with books, videos, and exhibits.

sights.name: Honmyo-ji Temple
sights.description: Nichiren sect temple and Kato Kiyomasa's family temple, with a registered Niomon and his mausoleum.

sights.name: Takahashi Inari Shrine
sights.description: One of Japan's five Inari shrines, known for business prosperity and the February Hatsuumo Festival.

sights.name: Kato Shrine
sights.description: Shrine in Kumamoto Castle to Kato Kiyomasa; Seishoko Festival is the fourth Sunday of July.

sights.name: Kumamoto Castle Inari Shrine
sights.description: Inari shrine near Kumamoto Castle, invited in 1588 as guardian deity, called Shirahige-san.

sights.name: Honmyo-ji Kato Kiyomasa Memorial Museum
sights.description: About 1,400 Kato Kiyomasa relics and cultural properties displayed at Honmyo-ji. Currently closed.

sights.name: Gakurin-ji Temple
sights.description: Soto Zen temple built in 757-764, with the grave of former castle lord Jo Chikamasa.

sights.name: Fujisaki Hachimangu Shrine
sights.description: Said to be Kumamoto's guardian shrine to Emperor Ojin, with a famous September festival.

sights.name: Kitaoka Shrine
sights.description: Historic shrine near Kumamoto Station, founded in 934, with a camphor tree over 600 years old.

sights.name: Lafcadio Hearn's Former Kumamoto Residence
sights.description: House where Lafcadio Hearn lived his first year teaching English in 1891, now a memorial museum.

sights.name: Meiju Bridge
sights.description: Stone arch bridge over the Tsuboi River built in 1877, said to be by Hashimoto Kangoro.

sights.name: Former Hosokawa Gyobu Residence
sights.description: 1646 home of Tadatoshi's brother, relocated and a prefectural important cultural property. Now closed.

sights.name: Kumamoto University Fifth High School Memorial Museum
sights.description: Red-brick 1889 Fifth High School where Hearn and Soseki taught, a national important cultural property.

sights.name: Riddell and Wright Memorial Museum
sights.description: On the site of Hannah Riddell's Hansen's disease institute, showing hospital photos and belongings.

sights.name: Natsume Soseki Uchitsuboi Former Residence
sights.description: Soseki's sixth Kumamoto home, lived in for one year and eight months, showing replica manuscripts.

sights.name: Kami-Kumamoto Station
sights.description: Opened in 1891 as Ikeda Station, where Natsume Soseki arrived; its 1913 wooden building now serves city trams.

sights.name: Kumamoto Castle
sights.description: One of Japan's three great castles, built by Kato Kiyomasa from 1601, and famous for cherry blossoms.

sights.name: Fureai no Shinrin Shinrin Gakushu Kan
Ono Sensui Park
sights.description: Park linked to Ono no Komachi; legend says its spring was her first bath. Statue, poem stone, and fireflies.

sights.name: Zuigan-ji Ruins
sights.description: Abandoned temple with a Jizo hall, Buddha images, paintings, and stone statues; grounds are now a park.

sights.name: Toge no Chaya Park and Museum
sights.description: Rebuilt teahouse on Torigoe Pass, said to model Soseki's Kusamakura, with a museum inside.

sights.name: Kihara Fudoson
sights.description: Called one of Japan's three great Fudo temples, linked to Saicho and Minamoto no Tametomo.

sights.name: Ungan-ji
sights.description: Zen temple known as Iwato Kannon, founded in 1351, with Musashi's writing cave behind it.

sights.name: Five Hundred Arhats
sights.description: Stone Buddhas at Ungan-ji, carved from 1779 over 24 years, each with a different expression.

sights.name: Reigando Cave
sights.description: Cave behind Ungan-ji where Musashi, invited to Higo in 1640, wrote the Book of Five Rings.

sights.name: Tabaruzaka Satsuma Rebellion Museum
sights.description: Museum on the Tabaruzaka battlefield of the Satsuma Rebellion, displaying weapons, relics, and dioramas.

sights.name: Yokoi Shonan Memorial Hall (Shijiken)
sights.description: Former home of thinker Yokoi Shonan, where he taught and Sakamoto Ryoma visited; restored in 1982.

sights.name: Kumamoto Prefectural Office Promenade
sights.description: Ginkgo-lined main-gate promenade that turns gold in autumn, with night lighting, popular for photos.

sights.name: Ezu Lake
sights.description: About 50-hectare spring-fed lake with steady temperatures, rich wildlife, boating, fishing, and walks.

sights.name: Musashizuka Park
sights.description: One of Miyamoto Musashi's graves; said buried standing in armor. Bronze statue, Japanese garden, teahouse, and early-May azaleas.

sights.name: Suizenji Jojuen (Suizenji Park)
sights.description: National scenic and historic stroll garden from 1632. Cherries bloom along paths from late March to early April.

sights.name: Kengun Shrine
sights.description: One of four Aso shrines; Kumamoto City's oldest. Famous as the Satsuma Rebellion departure point for Kumamoto troops.

sights.name: Miso Tenjin
sights.description: Japan's only miso deity shrine, founded in 713 during an epidemic. Said to have restored spoiled miso at Kokubunji.

sights.name: Goto Zezan Memorial Museum
sights.description: Former home of journalist and haiku poet Goto Zezan, now a public memorial museum displaying letters, paintings, and hanging scrolls.

sights.name: Kumamoto Museum of Literature and History
sights.description: Renewed in 2016, displaying modern literary materials of writers linked to Kumamoto and Edo-to-Meiji historical documents.

sights.name: Mount Kinpo
sights.description: Western counterpart to Mount Aso, main peak of the Kinpo range at about 665 meters, one of Higo's three mountains.

sights.name: Tabaruzaka Park
sights.description: Satsuma Rebellion battlefield, now a park with spring cherries and azaleas, a museum of weapons, and a memorial tower.

sights.name: Izumi Shrine
sights.description: Shrine founded in 1878 after the Satsuma Rebellion, with Suizenji Jojuen in its grounds, enshrining Hosokawa lords and Gracia.

sights.name: Nanamoto Government Army Cemetery
sights.description: Graves of over 300 Kumamoto Garrison soldiers killed in 1877 battles, recording rank, name, unit, and birthplace.

sights.name: Kitasenbaba Former Residence
sights.description: Natsume Soseki's seventh and last Kumamoto home, April to July 1900. The second-floor study remains. Currently closed.

sights.name: Yokoi Shonan and Restoration Statues
sights.description: Forceful bronze statue of Yokoi Shonan in Takahashi Park near Kumamoto Castle, a late-Edo pioneer of Japan's path.

sights.name: Statue of Lord Kato Kiyomasa
sights.description: Bronze statue of Kato Kiyomasa, builder of Kumamoto Castle, one of Japan's three great castles, in Sankaku Park.

sights.name: Kengun Self-Defense Force Street
sights.description: About 300 Somei-Yoshino trees line 1.5 km north of the Kengun tram terminus. Blooms from late March to early April.

sights.name: Kiyomizu Temple
sights.description: Temple at the foot of Hanaokayama behind Kumamoto Station. Tendai sect; principal image Senju Kannon. Formally Hase-dera.

sights.name: Sanken-do

sights.name: Onari Shrine

sights.name: Ayunose Bridge

sights.name: Koichiryo Shrine
sights.description: Shrine enshrined for over 1,000 years, known for hidden hearts and as a love-fulfillment shrine.

sights.name: Mamihara Bridge
sights.description: Bridge over the Gokase River between husband-and-wife rocks at former post town Mamihara; lip-shaped design won a 1995 award.

sights.name: Ryugu Falls
sights.description: About 20-meter two-tier falls beside Ryugu Falls Power Station in Yamato Town. Rear cave said to connect to Ryugu.

sights.name: Yatsushiro Shrine (Myoken-gu)
sights.description: Founded in 1186. UNESCO-listed November Myoken Festival draws over 100,000; a prefectural cultural property.

sights.name: Yatsushiro Castle Ruins
sights.description: Built in 1619 by Kato Masakata. Stone walls and moat remain; a national historic site and cherry-blossom spot.

sights.name: Matsui Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Matsui Yasuyuki and Okinaga in the castle's north bailey. Noted for 400-year-old Garyubai plum.

sights.name: Site of Miyazaki Hachiro's Death
sights.description: Miyazaki Hachiro, 27, died here on April 6, 1877, aiding Saigo's army in the Satsuma Rebellion.

sights.name: Thirteen-story Stone Pagoda
sights.description: National Important Cultural Property built in 1230, now eleven tiers, 6.6 meters, with Buddha and demon carvings.

sights.name: Yatsushiro Municipal Museum Mirai no Mori Museum
sights.description: Designed by Toyo Ito. Exhibits Yatsushiro history, Matsui heirlooms, Yatsushiro ware and festival materials. Currently closed.

sights.name: Former Gunchiku Shinden Sluice Gate A
sights.description: Sole surviving original Meiji sluice of the Gunchiku reclamation, among Japan's largest. National Important Cultural Property.

sights.name: Shohinken
sights.description: Tea garden built in 1688 by Matsui Naoyuki for his mother. About 9,000 square meters; a national scenic site.

sights.name: Sakamoto Hachiryu Observatory
sights.description: At about 500 meters elevation, with views of Yatsushiro, Amakusa, Uto Peninsula and Unzen, plus telescopes and a planetarium.

sights.name: Hikawa Dam
sights.description: About 200 Someiyoshino and 100 mountain cherries bloom by the lake. Bait and lure fishing are possible.

sights.name: Hinagu Onsen Shrine
sights.description: Built in 1420 for hot-spring deity Ichikishima-hime, with fine carvings. Spring cherry spot and summer shiranui viewpoint.

sights.name: Gokanosho Heike Village
sights.description: Theme facility on the Heike refugee legend, with a museum, Noh stage and thatched restaurant.

sights.name: Saza House
sights.description: Said to be Sugawara no Michizane's eldest son's hideaway, renamed Saza Taro, with plum-crest openwork.

sights.name: Sekishokan
sights.description: Displays Taneyama stonemason and stone-bridge materials in Toyo, their birthplace. The round tuff building is Artpolis-recognized.

sights.name: Momigi Suspension Bridges
sights.description: Two suspension bridges in Gokanosho, Ayatori and Shakunage, once local paths, with a nearby viewpoint.

sights.name: Sendan Todoro Falls
sights.description: One of Japan's 100 waterfalls, falling 70 meters; a suspension bridge reaches its 8-meter basin.

sights.name: Umenoki Todoro Falls
sights.description: A 38-meter waterfall named for a plum tree dropped while being carried; a bridge reaches the basin.

sights.name: Kasamatsu Bridge Park
sights.description: Toyo's largest stone bridge, 22.75 meters long, said to have been built by Hashimoto Kangoro.

sights.name: Shakain Temple
sights.description: A Tendai temple famous for Japan's longest stone stairway of 3,333 steps, founded in 799.

sights.name: Ogata House
sights.description: Restored home of a Heike descendant from about 300 years ago, with a hearth room and hidden room.

sights.name: Mizushima
sights.description: A small bridged island near the Kuma River mouth, designated a national scenic site in 2009.

sights.name: Hashirimizu Falls
sights.description: A roughly 100-meter waterfall on the Hashirimizu River in Sakamoto, Yatsushiro, also called Shirataki, long known as a scenic spot.

sights.name: Gokanosho
sights.description: Secluded Yatsushiro area ringed by 1,300-1,700 meter mountains, with a Heike warrior legend and vivid autumn foliage.

sights.name: Omatsuri Dendenkan
sights.description: Yatsushiro center presenting local folk performing arts, with a three-screen Myoken Festival theater.

sights.name: Kumamon Port Yatsushiro
sights.description: International cruise gateway with about 2.7 hectares of Kumamon park, a 6-meter statue, and 54 chorus statues.

sights.name: Catholic Yatsushiro Church
sights.description: Reportedly 6,000 Christians in 1588. First Edo-period martyr came from Yatsushiro in 1603. Founded in 1890.

sights.name: Yatsushiro Convent of the Sisters of St. Paul of Chartres
sights.description: White and blue building constructed in 1900. Surviving original structure was designated a National Registered Tangible Cultural Property in 2000.

sights.name: Ushio Shrine and Sai Shrine

sights.name: Ichifusayama Jingu Lower Shrine (Satomiya Shrine)
sights.description: Shrine for people unable to climb to the main shrine on Mount Ichifusa.

sights.name: Shitamachi Bridge
sights.description: Historic single-arch stone bridge in Yunomae, built in 1906, about 17 meters long and 3 meters wide; town cultural property.

sights.name: Josen-ji (Joshin-ji)
